output.brief:
The rejects come from one combination: Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's dryer (D5), which is running with a poor dew point. Arnholt arrives wetter (about 0.27–0.33% moisture, against a 0.20% limit). D5 can't dry it enough, so it reaches the press too wet, which causes splay and cracked latches. Arnholt on Press 7's healthy dryer runs at 0.8% rejects. Quillan on D5 runs at 0.9%. Arnholt through D5 runs at about 10%. When the same Arnholt lot was dried in a good portable dryer and fed to Press 5, rejects fell to 0.8%. The second-shift gap is explained by Press 5 being the only press that runs VX on that shift. New and experienced operators have the same rates on each resin, so the operators are not the cause. Don't discipline them. Dropping Arnholt isn't needed.

What to do this week: repair D5's heater and desiccant, confirm -40 °C, and restore the alarm limit. Until then, keep Arnholt off D5. Add a moisture check at the press for every resin lot. One open question remains: whether the annex storage makes Arnholt wetter. Every Arnholt sample came from the annex, so supplier and storage can't be separated. Test that separately before paying to move stock. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis.
